# Automated Embedding (autoEmbed) quantization types including binaryNoRescore — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Automated Embedding (autoEmbed) quantization types including binaryNoRescore. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-24 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Independent background evidence: the Hugging Face/mixedbread quantization experiment reports roughly 92.5% retained retrieval performance without binary rescoring versus about 96% with rescoring. It uses float-query/binary-document rescoring, so these figures do not benchmark Atlas binaryNoRescore or its full-precision rescoring alternative. (low confidence) — https://huggingface.co/blog/embedding-quantization

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The autoEmbed quantization field accepts float, scalar, binary, and binaryNoRescore; scalar is the default. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md · keywords: Automated Embedding (autoEmbed) quantization types including binaryNoRescore · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongoid/blob/master/lib/mongoid/fields.rb
- [statement] For autoEmbed, float stores 32-bit values. Scalar uses model-provided int8 values and approximately one quarter of float embedding storage and RAM. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md · keywords: Automated Embedding (autoEmbed) quantization types including binaryNoRescore · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md
- [statement] For autoEmbed, binary indexes one-bit values but retains full-precision vectors for candidate rescoring. MongoDB states RAM use is about 1/24 of float; this is not a corresponding total disk-storage reduction. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md · keywords: Automated Embedding (autoEmbed) quantization types including binaryNoRescore · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md
- [statement] binaryNoRescore uses model-provided one-bit vectors without rescoring. MongoDB describes faster queries and lower storage cost than binary, with lower accuracy; it gives no universal latency or recall improvement. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md · keywords: Automated Embedding (autoEmbed) quantization types including binaryNoRescore · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md
- [statement] MongoDB server documentation lists default similarity as dotProduct for float, cosine for scalar, and euclidean for binary and binaryNoRescore. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md · keywords: Automated Embedding (autoEmbed) quantization types including binaryNoRescore · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md
- [statement] Mongoid auto_embed_field accepts quantization and passes it into the autoEmbed index field specification. DRIVERS-3389 tracks the builder/type support required to expose these index options through language drivers. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-24) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongoid/blob/master/lib/mongoid/fields.rb · keywords: Automated Embedding (autoEmbed) quantization types including binaryNoRescore · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/DRIVERS-3389
- [statement] Scope boundary: Percona documents a self-managed autoEmbed pipeline whose Ollama model catalog sets quantization to float. This is evidence of a separate implementation context, not verification of Atlas binaryNoRescore support or performance. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-01) — https://docs.percona.com/percona-search-for-mongodb/configure-automatic-embedding-ollama.html
